summary: The core is organised around the real TMS34010 bus: it services the CPU's actual cycle types (word read/write, screen-refresh, VRAM shift-register memory-to-register/register-to-memory transfers) and builds display fetch and auto-erase from those cycles, where MAME uses scanline and shift-register callbacks with memcpy. The DMA blitter is a per-pixel address-counter engine with a two-term mode decode and models CPU/DMA bus contention, rather than a copy of MAME's 16-case switch and clipping code. A lot of the design is FPGA plumbing (DDR row remapping with copy-on-write, line buffers), which is neutral. There are few signs of schematic-level structure (no PAL equations or board net names), and one pitch expression matches MAME exactly, so the lean is moderate.

findings.signal: Video fetch driven by TMS34010 screen-refresh cycles
findings.note: Each line is loaded when the CPU issues a SCREEN_REFRESH bus cycle. The start address is built from the cycle's SRF address, DPYTAP and screen-origin outputs (sa/tap/org), as the VRAM serial port is loaded on the board. MAME instead reads params->rowaddr/coladdr in a per-scanline callback.

findings.signal: VRAM shift-register transfers as bus cycles
findings.note: PIXEL_MTR/PIXEL_RTM cycles act on whole 2-line VRAM rows (row = addr[20:13]) through a shift-register model, following real VRAM row transfers. MAME memcpy's 1024 words in TMS device callbacks.

Auto-erase is a two-step operation: MTR from row 0xFF (lines 510/511), then RTM into the row just displayed. Rows advance as line_load changes the displayed row, which is how the board does it with serial-register transfers. MAME copies line 510+(scanline&1) per scanline with memcpy.

Image-ROM reads return 0xFFFF while the DMA owns the ROM bus. CPU VRAM cycles are held off (vblock) or granted by pausing the DMA (cpause/cgrant). MAME's dma_w draws instantly and does not model this.
The draw/substitute decision is two small boolean terms on ctrl[3:0] for zero vs non-zero pixels. MAME has a 16-way switch with a separate loop per command.

findings.signal: Blitter as address counters, not clip-and-loop
findings.note: For hflip, the source address counts down from the start address while the destination counts up. X/Y use 9-bit wrapping counters, and there is no port of MAME's code that adjusts gfxoffset -= (width-1)*8 and xpos += width-1 or its explicit X/Y clipping blocks.
pitch = (offset +/- hsize + 3) & ~3 is the same expression as MAME's rowbytes = (rowbytes +/- width + 3) & ~3, including the sign flip for hflip.

Chip selects are equality tests on 7 high address bits, as a decoder PAL would do, and they mirror. They are not MAME's 32-bit ranges. CMOS writes are gated by the coin-door switch (in1[11]) and addr[14], not by MAME's cmos_enable_w latch.

findings.signal: Sound boards decoded like a '138 with chip-select banking
findings.note: I/O is selected by A[12:10] with strobes that fire on chip-select regardless of R/W (comm_st, cvsd_clk). ROM banking is expressed as chip-select bits plus address lines, not MAME's computed bank offsets.
Two biquad stages and a high-pass stage model the board's output filtering, and the instance name u_c43 is a component reference. MAME routes the HC55516 straight to the mixer.

findings.signal: DMA register file and status bit
findings.note: The register order (ctrl, offset, src lo/hi, x, y, w, h, palette, color), busy in bit 15 and the IRQ cleared on a ctrl write are the programming interface. Any correct core must match them.

findings.signal: FPGA VRAM remapping/COW and line buffers
findings.note: Row remap tables with reference counts and copy-on-write, plus DDR line buffers, are resource engineering so DDR can emulate VRAM row transfers. They count neither way.
